problem: Standard split conformal prediction pools steps as if exchangeable, but VLN steps within an episode are dependent, variable-length and causally linked, so it undercovers and often collapses to the argmax action, giving no route-level guarantee.
motivation: Agents need calibrated, distribution-free signals of when to defer to a human before errors compound; softmax confidence is not calibrated and existing help-request heads are heuristic. A CP scheme that calibrates over whole episodes could give set sizes usable as an act-or-ask trigger.
key_idea: Rescale each step's nonconformity score by the policy's residual confidence (divide by 2-pmax) and calibrate one maximum score per episode, so that exchangeability of episodes yields simultaneous coverage of the ground-truth action at every step with probability at least 1-alpha.
insight: Making the whole episode the calibration unit (max over steps) is what restores alpha-sensitivity: step-pooled base CP undercovers in almost every entry (e.g., DUET R2R THR alpha=0.30 base 0.608 vs ENCP 0.897) and collapses to singleton sets. The parameter-free weight matches the learned weight in coverage with smaller sets (Table 2), so the gain comes from episode-level calibration rather than the learned normalization. The cost is much larger sets (DUET R2R alpha=0.10 mean size 6.7), and coverage guarantees are lost under seen-to-unseen shift.
method: Episode-level calibration: compute the max over steps of the normalized score of the ground-truth action per calibration episode, then take the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))-th order statistic as the threshold.
Base scores: THR (1-p), deterministic APS (U=0), and RAPS (lambda=0.1, k_reg=2), applied to the policy's action probabilities over admissible actions including STOP.
Parameter-free normalization: s_norm = s_base/(2-pmax), which preserves the action ranking but raises the effective threshold when the policy is less confident.

Learning-based weight: a 2x32 ReLU MLP with softplus output predicts w from entropy, pmax, top-2 gap, log|A|, t/Tmax and alpha; it is trained on one calibration half with target clip((1-p(a*))/(1-pmax),0,10), and the quantile is calibrated on the disjoint other half.
Deployment: the raw set is thresholded at q-hat; an empty set falls back to the argmax action; the agent asks for help when the deployed set size exceeds a budget tau.
Theory: Theorem 1 gives P(all steps covered) >= 1-alpha under episode exchangeability, and a corollary gives step-averaged coverage >= 1-alpha; a proposition characterizes when the threshold is zero.

setting.backbone: DUET, HAMT, Recurrent VLN-BERT (PREVALENT and OSCAR init) policies, frozen; ENCP is a post-hoc wrapper (optional small MLP weight in the learned variant)
setting.training_data: Policies are pre-trained on the standard R2R/REVERIE data; the ENCP parameter-free variant needs no training and calibrates on val-seen episodes; the learned-weight MLP is fit on half of the val-seen calibration episodes.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB on Matterport3D navigation graph, with instruction and history (as used by each policy)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints plus STOP (DUET also includes global frontier nodes)
setting.privileged: Calibration uses ground-truth (teacher) actions from val-seen episodes; the simulated help experiment uses an oracle assistant with the goal and full navigation graph.

numbers_note: Paper reports conformal coverage and set-size metrics rather than SR/SPL. Only representative entries are listed; Table 1 has all policies, scores and alpha levels (0.10/0.20/0.30). Trajectory-coverage results are in figures only.
results: ENCP meets the step-coverage target 1-alpha for all four policies, three scores and three alpha levels on R2R and REVERIE val-unseen, whereas step-pooled base CP undercovers in every R2R entry and for REVERIE DUET (e.g., DUET R2R THR alpha=0.30: 0.608 vs 0.897). Set-size-triggered oracle help raises DUET R2R success from 71.2% to 76.9% at a 6.4% ask rate and to 91.1% at 32.3%.
limitations: Coverage is guaranteed only under episode exchangeability; the seen-to-unseen shift is outside this premise, and trajectory-level coverage falls below target there (only HAMT-REVERIE exceeds it).

ENCP sets are large (e.g., 6.7 actions for DUET), and one hard step can set the whole episode's score. The help-seeking study uses a simulated oracle and a tau swept on val-unseen, with no human operators.
Assumes a finite discrete action space; it does not cover continuous VLN.
